Gridded H19 radar for merging with gauges

Source: R/h19.R
h19_radar.Rd

H19 radar comes as daily NetCDF files, each holding that day's 15-minute accumulations on British National Grid, in year and month folders. Sixteen years of it will not fit in memory at once. h19_radar() indexes the files (the time of every layer in every file), crops them to an extent around the catchment and its gauges, and returns a reader that gives one step's grid when asked, loading each daily file once as the steps are read in order. Pass its radar and grid to merge_rainfall().

Usage

h19_radar(files, extent, varname = NULL, fallback_crs = "EPSG:27700")

Arguments

files

Paths of the daily NetCDF files, in any order; they are sorted by time.

extent

Numeric c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) in British National Grid metres.

varname

Name of the radar variable; by default found in each file among the H19 names.

fallback_crs

Coordinate reference system assumed when a file does not state one.

Value

A list of class pdm_h19 with grid (cell-centre x and y, both increasing), time (the time of every step, POSIXct in UTC), radar (a function of the step number returning that step's grid, mm, as a matrix of length(grid$x) rows by length(grid$y) columns) and index (the file and layer of every step).

Details

Variable names. The archive uses "radar rain-accum H19" for 2010 to 2019 and "rainfall_radar_amount" from 2021. By default each file's variable is found among these; name another with varname.

Times are read from each file's time variable and its units, such as "minutes since 1970-01-01 00:00:00", in UTC. Check whether they mark the start or the end of each accumulation, and align the gauges to match: an hour's offset moves every peak.

Extent. Crop to a box that holds the catchment and the gauges used with it, with a margin: the merged field needs radar at every gauge. Cells with no radar value are NA, and a merged step that needs one is NA.

See also

merge_rainfall(), catchment_mask()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
files <- list.files("F:/.../01_H19", pattern = "\\.nc$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
h19 <- h19_radar(files, extent = c(290000, 330000, 120000, 160000))
mask <- catchment_mask(h19$grid$x, h19$grid$y, boundary)
merged <- merge_rainfall(gauges, gauge_rain, h19$grid, mask, radar = h19$radar,
                         method = "conditional")
} # }
